prompts:
Use case: ui-mockup. Produce a polished landscape concept image for netKonnect. Minimal colorful line art on pure white, thin dark blue-gray outlines, restrained lime, teal, sky blue, warm coral and ochre flat fills, abundant whitespace. Small settlements grow with cumulative recorded download + upload bytes, not instantaneous rate. Bicycles become two-wheel hand pushcarts carrying wood; trucks become pickups with open beds full of building supplies; planes drop parachute crates. All data is illustrative. Legible sans-serif typography. No photographic texture, gradients, heavy shadows, game HUD, isometric 3D rendering, or excessive decoration. Preserve direction: Download travels left toward the application; Upload travels right toward service. The illustration is a static mockup of slow gentle movement.
Asset: compact service dashboard. A polished desktop UI with a slim left sidebar branded netKonnect, Overview selected. Title: Service cities. Subtitle: Built from total data. Three generous service rows, application on left, dual traffic lanes through middle, miniature colorful settlement immediately beside service label on right, numeric total on far right. Row 1 Firefox to YouTube, 128 GB, Metropolis: tiny tall towers, plane over service dropping supply crate by parachute. Row 2 OneDrive to OneDrive, 8.4 GB, Village: a cluster of cottages and a shop, supply pickup on lane. Row 3 Code to GitHub, 180 MB, House: one simple house, hand pushcart stacked with wood on lane. Include small Download and Upload lane arrows, crisp totals, plenty of breathing room. Illustrations deliberately small and fine, visual hierarchy keeps service names clear. Footer: Illustrative data. Compact table-like UI grounded in a white network observatory desktop app.

Use case: infographic-diagram. Landscape concept sheet titled Every byte builds. Seven evenly spaced individual miniature settlements across the upper-middle in a clear labeled sequence, ensure ALL SEVEN: Shack, House, Mansion, Neighborhood, Village, City, Metropolis. Architecture grows in both density and height: humble wooden shed, standalone cottage, larger stately home, suburban cluster, village with shop and clock tower, dense midrise city, tall skyscraper skyline. Consistent delicate dark blue-gray line art, small flat patches of lime, teal, sky blue, coral and ochre. Pure white background, very generous whitespace, minimal architecture, no texture, no gradients or 3D realism. No numerical thresholds. Below the progression show three larger clean illustrations with labels: Pushcart — small two-wheel hand cart piled with wooden planks; Supply pickup — a pickup with open bed full of crates, timber, and building supplies; Airdrop — a small propeller cargo plane releasing a crate on a parachute above a tiny building. Show thin fine outlines and a few colorful surfaces. Elegant editorial product design sheet, not a children's poster. Bottom notes: City size = total data. Vehicle activity = current traffic. Single consistent stroke weight, very readable short labels.

Asset: roomier service diorama dashboard layout. Title: Service cities. Three horizontally stacked spacious rounded cards, clean white desktop UI. Each card: small application icon and app name at far left, two thin parallel supply traffic lanes through the middle, colorful line-art settlement occupying right third anchored at lane endpoint next to readable service label and total. Row 1 Firefox to YouTube, 128 GB, Metropolis: group of slender skyscrapers, smaller foreground buildings, small lime plane dropping TWO crates on parachutes above settlement. Row 2 OneDrive to OneDrive, 8.4 GB, Village: small cottages, shop, two simple trees, loaded sky-blue supply pickup on road. Row 3 Code to GitHub, 180 MB, House: simple coral cottage, a wood stack beside it, ochre hand pushcart full of wood on road. Settlements look like light architectural sketches in elevation with slight depth cues, no ground islands or 3D game worlds. City illustrations bigger than compact table but still sparse. Small Download left arrow and Upload right arrow for lanes. Very subtle pale-gray card borders. Footer: Illustrative data. Total data builds the city; live traffic delivers.
roomierLayoutCorrection: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the last image, the three-row Service cities dashboard. Keep ALL text, layout, cities, colors, planes, parachutes, icons, pickups, whitespace and outlines exactly as they are. Change ONLY every cyclist/bicycle-and-trailer illustration into a person WALKING and pushing a small two-wheel HAND PUSHCART piled with wooden planks or logs. In each Upload lane use a wooden handcart with two side wheels and two handles, a walking worker on the left pushing it right. The larger vehicle beside the GitHub house must also become a walking worker pushing a handcart of timber. No bicycle frames, pedals, saddles, riders sitting, bicycle wheels or trailers attached to cycles anywhere. The wheels belong only to the cart. Same small minimal colorful line-art styling. Every download pickup must face left to match Download arrow; every upload handcart must move right to match Upload arrow. Preserve all other elements.
